main_text.p: ro habuisti. D. Imò seruus meus est. Q. Utrum liber, an seruus sit? R. Quia temporis tantum causa id feci, ut portiorum avaritiam vitarem. F. At quacunque ratione feceris, tamen eum pro libero habuisti, haberique voluisti. D. An seruus, quem dominus temporis tantum causa pro libero haberi voluit, cuique idcirco libertatis insignia tradidit, liber sit. quod quoniam ad disceptandum perquàm difficile est, propterea Imp. Alexander rescripsit, voluntatis quaestionem in æstimatione iudicis esse. L.7.C.de fideicom. cuius rei exemplum

page.notes: Running head at top right is a dark decorated block; I could not read it. The mark in the left margin looks like handwriting, so I left it out. Long s is printed as f throughout (feruus, fit, eft, caufa, difceptandum); I have written it as s. The catchword "ex" sits at the right below the last line; I kept it out of the text. The printed word "haberiqúe" has an accent over the u; I have written "haberique" without it.
